Respondents Date of institution of Revision : 28/10/2022 Date on which Order reserved : 02/06/2025 Date on which Order pronounced : 04/06/2025  ORDER 1.
The present order shall decide the revision petition filed by Dinesh Kumar.

2. The facts in brief are that the complaint u/s 200 Cr.PC alongwith the application u/s 156(3) Cr.PC were filed on the ground that on 03/07/2021 his father in law Narendra Pal Singh, his son Jitendra,
his brother inlaw Rinku and his maternal in law alongwith his other relatives came to his house where is mother, bhabhi, his wife Ritu and his children were present.
In their absence they ransacked the house, gave beatings to his mother, looted jewelry and created ruckus.
When the complainant came to know about the incident, he called on 100 number from his factory.
Cr. Rev No.: 598/2022 Dinesh Kumar vs State & ors Page no. 2 of 7 PCR reached at the spot and took his mother and complainant reached at the PS.

entities.text: Cr. Rev No.: 598/2022 Dinesh Kumar vs State & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even there he was manhandled.
Complainant in order to save himself ran towards bypass.
The accused persons who were behind him, gave a blow on the head with some sharp edged article and fled away from the spot.
With the intervention of the local people, the complainant was saved.
The complainant was taken to the hospital where his MLC was prepared.
It is further alleged that on 31/07/2021 these very persons abused the brother of the complainant which was recorded.
Written complaint was given to the PS Burari on 10/08/2021 but no action was taken.
On 15/08/2021, the complainant was threatened on phone by the brother in law.
On 16/08/2021, another complaint was made at PS Burari which has been received vide DD No.84 but no action was taken.
It was thus, prayed that directions should be given to the Police Station to register FIR as the complaint discloses commission of cognizable offence.
3. Ld. MM called for action taken report from concerned PS.
As per the action taken report, inquiry was conducted.
During the course of the inquiry, it was revealed that there is matrimonial dispute between the complainant Dinesh and his wife Ritu.
It was further stated that FIR has been registered against him in Mahila Thana, Distt. Ghaziabad UP.
On the day of incident, both the parties were present in the house in order to resolve the issue which turned into arguments and scrimmage.
Both the parties arrived in PS Cr. Rev No.: 598/2022 Dinesh Kumar vs State & ors Page no. 3 of 7 where they stated that they would pursue the matter with CAW Cell.

Vide the impugned order dated 19/09/2022, ld. MM-09, Central/THC not only dismissed the application u/s 156(3) Cr.PC but also the complaint u/s 200 Cr.PC.
5.
It is this order against which revision has been filed before this court.
6. The perusal of the file shows that repeatedly adjournments have been sought.
The perusal of file shows that on 20/08/2023 adjournment was sought by the parties on the ground that the matter is likely to be settled.

On 07/10/2023, request was made that no settlement have been arrived at,
accordingly, the matter was posted for arguments.
On 16/12/2023 it was brought to the notice of the court that quashing petition was pending before Allahabad High Court.
Thereafter, again adjournment was sought.
7. Ld. counsel for the petitioner had again requested for adjournment on the ground that the daughter of the petitioner and respondents no.3 i.e. wife is admitted in the hospital.
She could not give any satisfactory explanation for non appearance of the counsel.

On the other hand, ld. Counsel for the respondents argued that the matter has been settled, and in Hon'ble Allahabad High Court vide its order dated 05/01/2024 has quashed the proceedings Cr. Rev No.: 598/2022 Dinesh Kumar vs State & ors Page no. 4 of 7 pending in the court of Ld. Civil Judge, Jr. Division, FTC- I, Ghaziabad u/s 498A/323/504/506 IPC, 34 DP Act, PS Mahila Thana.

entities.text: Civil Judge, Jr. Division, FTC- I, Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: She had also placed on record the copy of the order.
8. I have heard the counsels for the parties and perused the trial court record.

9. The Ld. MM, while deciding the application u/s 156(3) could not have dismissed the complaint and should have taken recourse to the provisions of section 200 Cr.PC to that extent the order of the Ld. MM is bad in law and was liable to be set aside.
However, in the given facts, once the matter was settled and parties are residing together, no useful purpose will be served to keep the present revision pending.
The revisionist did not disclose about the settlement or quashing of the proceedings by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court to this court.
10. In so far as the application u/s 156(3) Cr.PC was concerned.
There is no infirmity or illegality in the order of the Ld. MM, as the complainant himself is not sure whether his wife was present on 03/07/2021 in the house or she had come alongwith other persons.
The complaint dated 10/08/2021 which states that his wife was already present in the house.
Secondly, no MLC has been filed on record alongwith the complaint case.
No recording with respect to the incident dated 15/08/2021 has been filed.
Accordingly, the present revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
